item.title: UNC5342 NPM Malware Uses Custom Headers to Gate Malicious Payload
item.author: V0lundr
item.description:
UNC5342 NPM Malware Uses Custom Headers to Gate Malicious Payloads

While tracking DPRK-linked weaponised npm packages, I came across an unreported technique employed by UNC5342 to evade detection and analysis. The malicious package uses a conditional serving mechanism that delivers different responses based on request authentication — effectively hiding the malicious payload while remaining operational against targets.

UNC5342 Refines OtterCookie Delivery Chain with JsonSilo Infrastructure

While continuing to track DPRK-linked weaponised npm packages, I observed UNC5342 refining its delivery chain — pivoting away from Vercel infrastructure and adopting jsonsilo[.]com and npoint[.]io as payload staging points for the OtterCookie malware family.

item.title: Malicious Distribution of RMM Tools via Adobe-Themed Download Infrastructure
item.author: V0lundr
item.description:
Malicious Distribution of RMM Tools via Adobe-Themed Download Infrastructure

In March and April 2026, I observed a some spearphishing samples that were most likely a part of a phishing campaign targeting financial departments in Europe and across multiple sectors. The campaign directed victims to previously compromised websites hosting fake Adobe software that deployed Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) tools to establish access to victim systems. In one observed case, the phishing email, purporting to be a document pending to be signed, was delivered to the victim mailbox, passing email security filters (Exhibit 1).

item.title: From Invoice Lure to In-Memory Injection: Phantom Stealer via Donut and Heaven's Gate
item.author: V0lundr
item.description:
From Invoice Lure to In-Memory Injection

In January 2026, I identified a phishing campaign leveraging compromised supplier mailboxes and a multi-stage infection chain to deploy Phantom Stealer using obfuscated batch loaders, in-memory PowerShell decryption, Donut shellcode injection, and Heaven's Gate evasion. This post analyses the campaign's tradecraft, persistence mechanisms, and data exfiltration methods.

item.title: MuddyWater Weaponizes Word Macros in Targeted Campaign Delivering GhostFetch
item.author: V0lundr
item.description:
MuddyWater Weaponises Word Macros in Targeted Campaign Delivering GhostFetch

In February 2026, I identified a new phishing campaign associated with MuddyWater, framed as a travel reservation from Air Arabia. When recipients enable the document's embedded macro, it installs and executes the GhostFetch loader. This post analyses the campaign's lure design, delivery mechanism, and GhostFetch behaviour, and provides practical guidance for defenders.

item.title: Arabic Security-Training Lure Deploying a VBA Reverse Shell
item.author: V0lundr
item.description:
Arabic Security-Training Lure Deploying a VBA Reverse Shell

Introduction

In May 2026, I stumbled upon a weaponised Microsoft Word macro-enabled template (.dotm, 33,966 bytes, SHA-256 e6cc542b690066cf6914e88199ce234236f2d929f313af8b0b2f8babe43d4f7d) that surfaced through one of the VirusTotal hunting rule. The template carries an Arabic-language lure themed as a peer-to-peer review request for a "third security training course", stored as an AutoText entry rather than in the visible document body.
